answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. What this achieves is a system where the cost of an attack is public and provable, so the whole network can trust verdicts without trusting any single identity.
